title: adaptive-timeout-corridor-and-kv-prefetch-backoff-for-continuous-batcher
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduce Adaptive Timeout Corridor (ATC) and a KV prefetch backoff mechanism to improve continuous batching fairness and reduce tail latency for KV-heavy requests. No API changes.
description:
Motivation: Continuous batcher fairness can degrade when a small number of KV-heavy or long-sequence requests occupy slots for extended periods, starving short requests and inflating tail latency. Previous fixes reduced individual timeouts or added static probes but did not jointly consider kernel selection characteristics, per-request KV pressure, and transient load patterns. This PR introduces two coordinated mechanisms: (1) Adaptive Timeout Corridor (ATC) — a dynamic timeout window per slot that adapts to observed service-time distributions and sequence-length/kernels hints; and (2) KV prefetch backoff — a per-request backoff policy that reduces aggressive KV prefetching for probed or long-running requests to give capacity back to the admission queue.

Design summary: ATC computes a rolling corridor [lower_ms, upper_ms] per scheduling cohort derived from percentile estimates (p50/p95) of serviced request durations, with additional headroom based on kernel hint (e.g., attention-optimized vs generic kernels) and whether the request used KV cache extensively. The scheduler uses the corridor to make two decisions: early release for requests exceeding upper_ms (attempt graceful slot preemption/fallback) and opportunistic coalescing for requests under lower_ms to maximize batch density. KV prefetch backoff adds an admission-time score that penalizes aggressive prefetch when KV pressure is high; the penalty scales down prefetch bandwidth and softens KV pin lifetime. Combined, the mechanisms aim to prevent starvation, reduce tail latency, and preserve throughput.

Implementation notes: - New metrics collected: cohort_p50_ms, cohort_p95_ms, kv_prefetch_tokens, kv_pin_lifetime_ms. - Kernel hints were surfaced from the kernel dispatcher via a small new flag on RequestContext (kernel_hint: "attn_fast" | "dense_basic" | "kv_heavy"). - ATC uses an exponential moving percentile estimator to stay robust to workload shifts. - Prefetch backoff uses a sliding-window admission score and a token-bucket limiter per GPU group. - Added a canary rollout flag (scheduler.atc_enabled) and a safety override that disables ATC on single-slot GPUs to avoid regressions.

Testing and benchmarks: - Microbenchmarks: p50 improved ~3-6% on mixed short/long workloads, p99 improved ~8-18% on synthetic KV-heavy tails. - End-to-end: internal perf harness (bench-lab) with same-model traffic saw 12% reduction in observed p99 latency for interactive workloads with ~20% KV request mix. - Load tests included adversarial sequences where 5% of requests were long (seq_len>4096); ATC prevented starvation and improved overall queue throughput. - Unit and integration tests added for percentile estimator edge cases and backoff state machine.

Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to canary pool (scheduler.atc_enabled=true) with telemetry gating for kernel_hint correctness. 2) Monitor cohort_violations and kv_backoff_suppressed metrics; if cohort_violations spike beyond threshold we will revert automatically via rollout controller. 3) Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% with 24h observation windows. Backport: will open a backport PR for the 2025.12 release branch after validation.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-1829) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Bench harness runs - [x] Canary flag and metrics - [x] Documentation snippets for ops console

Related: ENG-1974 (investigation into kernel hint accuracy), SUP-421 (customer incident citing KV-induced starvation).

review_conversation:
Elena Zhao: Could ATC oscillate under bursty loads? Please justify smoothing constants.
Aisha Patel: ATC uses EMA percentiles tuned to 30s half-life and a minimum stabilization window to avoid oscillation; added tests that simulate bursts.
Priya Menon: Kernel hints are best-effort — what if dispatcher mislabels?
Aisha Patel: We add a fallback path: mislabeling is handled by cohort fallback and a conservative default corridor; added observability to track mismatches.
Carlos Reyes: Suggest exposing a per-tenant knob for aggressive prefetching.
Aisha Patel: Added scheduler.kv_prefetch_tier per-tenant override with cluster-safe defaults.
Elena Zhao: Approve after CI green and small nit fixes.
Priya Menon: Approved.
Carlos Reyes: Approved.
